### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 375

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `applyLocalTrimFallback` reports success unconditionally — consider the under-trigger check `_runPass` uses**

```dart
hooks.onDone(pass, tokensAfter);
return true;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

```dart
return (
  done: true,
  success:
      !shouldCompact(tokensAfter, window, settings) &&
      !_overMessageCap(),
);
```

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure), so suggestion-level — but either mirroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional would keep the two valves honest in the same way.

`AutoCompactor.run()` deliberately rethrows a cancelled run token (issue #1085 round-4):

`applyLocalTrimFallback` is now a public, host-callable API and does not check `runToken`: if the owning run's token cancels around the same moment the total budget fires, the trim still applies and reports success on a run the user aborted. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: CHANGELOG wording overstates what this branch covers**

> a structured compaction that hits its budget watchdog (300s total, **or a provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from**)

The `outcome.timedOut` branch fires **only** on the `TimeoutException` raised by `running.timeout(totalBudget, …)` in `_runStructured` — i.e. the total-budget watchdog. A provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from surfaces as `ok: false, timedOut: false` and takes the pre-existing fall-through to the classic engine (whose own `_runPass` ladder already ends on the local trim). The session survives in both shapes, but via different valves; as written the entry attributes the second shape to this change. # pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,

flutter analyze+tests;

  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,

  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());

```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue

— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual failure path (timeout + nothing droppable) still skips `hooks.onDone` — the host bracket stays open**

The rescue path now closes the `onDone` bracket correctly (and the new test pins `doneCount == 1`), but the residual failure branch this PR rewrote still terminates without `onDone`:

```dart

  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
);
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
return false;
```

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

- classic `_runPass` failure branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:479-500`): fires `onPass(ok: false)` **and** `onDone`;
- structured `ok` branch and the new trim path: fire `onDone`.

After this change, the timed-out-nothing-droppable path is the **only** terminal path that leaves the bracket open, and it has a concrete CLI consequence: `_AutoCompactorCliHooks.onDone` is what fires `_hep?.compactionEnd(...)` and clears `_runTokensBefore` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:192-207`, set in `onPass:122`, cleared **only** in `onDone:207`). A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

…and add `expect(hooks.doneCount, <expected>)` to the second test. Pre-existing gap, so not blocking — but it is a two-line-in-scope fix on a branch this PR owns.

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 375

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `applyLocalTrimFallback` reports success unconditionally — consider the under-trigger check `_runPass` uses**

```dart
hooks.onDone(pass, tokensAfter);
return true;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

```dart
return (
  done: true,
  success:
      !shouldCompact(tokensAfter, window, settings) &&
      !_overMessageCap(),
);
```

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure), so suggestion-level — but either mirroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional would keep the two valves honest in the same way.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 358

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runToken` cancellation parity — `run()` surfaces a user abort, this new public valve does not**

`AutoCompactor.run()` deliberately rethrows a cancelled run token (issue #1085 round-4):

```dart
} finally {
  // A cancelled compaction is NEVER a mere failed pass …
  runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
}
```

`applyLocalTrimFallback` is now a public, host-callable API and does not check `runToken`: if the owning run's token cancels around the same moment the total budget fires, the trim still applies and reports success on a run the user aborted. Today that is harmless — the CLI covers it (`_runAutoCompact`'s `finally { abort.token.throwIfCancelled(); }` plus the funnel's `_throwIfUserAborted()` gates), and `task_executor`/the Flutter app pass `runToken: null` — but a future host calling this method directly gets no such belt. Consider a `runToken?.throwIfCancelled()` at the top of the method (or in the factory's timed-out branch) for parity with the documented cancel contract.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: CHANGELOG wording overstates what this branch covers**

> a structured compaction that hits its budget watchdog (300s total, **or a provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from**)

The `outcome.timedOut` branch fires **only** on the `TimeoutException` raised by `running.timeout(totalBudget, …)` in `_runStructured` — i.e. the total-budget watchdog. A provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from surfaces as `ok: false, timedOut: false` and takes the pre-existing fall-through to the classic engine (whose own `_runPass` ladder already ends on the local trim). The session survives in both shapes, but via different valves; as written the entry attributes the second shape to this change. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

```dart

  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
);

hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
return false;
```

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

- classic `_runPass` failure branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:479-500`): fires `onPass(ok: false)` **and** `onDone`;
- structured `ok` branch and the new trim path: fire `onDone`.

After this change, the timed-out-nothing-droppable path is the **only** terminal path that leaves the bracket open, and it has a concrete CLI consequence: `_AutoCompactorCliHooks.onDone` is what fires `_hep?.compactionEnd(...)` and clears `_runTokensBefore` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:192-207`, set in `onPass:122`, cleared **only** in `onDone:207`). A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

…and add `expect(hooks.doneCount, <expected>)` to the second test. Pre-existing gap, so not blocking — but it is a two-line-in-scope fix on a branch this PR owns.

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 375

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `applyLocalTrimFallback` reports success unconditionally — consider the under-trigger check `_runPass` uses**

```dart
hooks.onDone(pass, tokensAfter);
return true;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

```dart
return (
  done: true,
  success:
      !shouldCompact(tokensAfter, window, settings) &&
      !_overMessageCap(),
);
```

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure), so suggestion-level — but either mirroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional would keep the two valves honest in the same way.

`AutoCompactor.run()` deliberately rethrows a cancelled run token (issue #1085 round-4):

`applyLocalTrimFallback` is now a public, host-callable API and does not check `runToken`: if the owning run's token cancels around the same moment the total budget fires, the trim still applies and reports success on a run the user aborted. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: CHANGELOG wording overstates what this branch covers**

> a structured compaction that hits its budget watchdog (300s total, **or a provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from**)

The `outcome.timedOut` branch fires **only** on the `TimeoutException` raised by `running.timeout(totalBudget, …)` in `_runStructured` — i.e. the total-budget watchdog. A provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from surfaces as `ok: false, timedOut: false` and takes the pre-existing fall-through to the classic engine (whose own `_runPass` ladder already ends on the local trim). The session survives in both shapes, but via different valves; as written the entry attributes the second shape to this change. # pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

blocks.text:
Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

```dart

hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());

```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

return (

By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap.
