# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual failure path (timeout + nothing droppable) still skips `hooks.onDone` — the host bracket stays open**

The rescue path now closes the `onDone` bracket correctly (and the new test pins `doneCount == 1`), but the residual failure branch this PR rewrote still terminates without `onDone`:

```dart

  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
);
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
return false;
```

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

- classic `_runPass` failure branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:479-500`): fires `onPass(ok: false)` **and** `onDone`;
- structured `ok` branch and the new trim path: fire `onDone`.

After this change, the timed-out-nothing-droppable path is the **only** terminal path that leaves the bracket open, and it has a concrete CLI consequence: `_AutoCompactorCliHooks.onDone` is what fires `_hep?.compactionEnd(...)` and clears `_runTokensBefore` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:192-207`, set in `onPass:122`, cleared **only** in `onDone:207`). A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

…and add `expect(hooks.doneCount, <expected>)` to the second test. Pre-existing gap, so not blocking — but it is a two-line-in-scope fix on a branch this PR owns.

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 375

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `applyLocalTrimFallback` reports success unconditionally — consider the under-trigger check `_runPass` uses**

```dart
hooks.onDone(pass, tokensAfter);
return true;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

```dart
return (
  done: true,
  success:
      !shouldCompact(tokensAfter, window, settings) &&
      !_overMessageCap(),
);
```

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure), so suggestion-level — but either mirroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional would keep the two valves honest in the same way.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 358

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runToken` cancellation parity — `run()` surfaces a user abort, this new public valve does not**

`AutoCompactor.run()` deliberately rethrows a cancelled run token (issue #1085 round-4):

```dart
} finally {
  // A cancelled compaction is NEVER a mere failed pass …
  runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
}
```

`applyLocalTrimFallback` is now a public, host-callable API and does not check `runToken`: if the owning run's token cancels around the same moment the total budget fires, the trim still applies and reports success on a run the user aborted. Today that is harmless — the CLI covers it (`_runAutoCompact`'s `finally { abort.token.throwIfCancelled(); }` plus the funnel's `_throwIfUserAborted()` gates), and `task_executor`/the Flutter app pass `runToken: null` — but a future host calling this method directly gets no such belt. Consider a `runToken?.throwIfCancelled()` at the top of the method (or in the factory's timed-out branch) for parity with the documented cancel contract.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: CHANGELOG wording overstates what this branch covers**

> a structured compaction that hits its budget watchdog (300s total, **or a provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from**)

The `outcome.timedOut` branch fires **only** on the `TimeoutException` raised by `running.timeout(totalBudget, …)` in `_runStructured` — i.e. the total-budget watchdog. A provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from surfaces as `ok: false, timedOut: false` and takes the pre-existing fall-through to the classic engine (whose own `_runPass` ladder already ends on the local trim). The session survives in both shapes, but via different valves; as written the entry attributes the second shape to this change. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart

hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

return (

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
  Flake intake consumes PR-dispatch runs only (gh-1537:
  `scripts/flake_watch.py` filters to `workflow_dispatch` events — the
  retired main trigger leaves SM validation dispatches and v* tag runs;
  a red tag run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish /
  ci-red-report, never quarantined as a flake). Dedup is per test name
  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1754
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1754
- **Title**: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1743` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +216
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T17:38:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T18:32:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 1032

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual failure path (timeout + nothing droppable) still skips `hooks.onDone` — the host bracket stays open**

The rescue path now closes the `onDone` bracket correctly (and the new test pins `doneCount == 1`), but the residual failure branch this PR rewrote still terminates without `onDone`:

```dart
final trimmed = build().applyLocalTrimFallback(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
);
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
return false;
```

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

- classic `_runPass` failure branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:479-500`): fires `onPass(ok: false)` **and** `onDone`;
- structured `ok` branch and the new trim path: fire `onDone`.

After this change, the timed-out-nothing-droppable path is the **only** terminal path that leaves the bracket open, and it has a concrete CLI consequence: `_AutoCompactorCliHooks.onDone` is what fires `_hep?.compactionEnd(...)` and clears `_runTokensBefore` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:192-207`, set in `onPass:122`, cleared **only** in `onDone:207`). A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

…and add `expect(hooks.doneCount, <expected>)` to the second test. Pre-existing gap, so not blocking — but it is a two-line-in-scope fix on a branch this PR owns.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1754._

> ℹ️ **4 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 1032

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: residual failure path (timeout + nothing droppable) still skips `hooks.onDone` — the host bracket stays open**

The rescue path now closes the `onDone` bracket correctly (and the new test pins `doneCount == 1`), but the residual failure branch this PR rewrote still terminates without `onDone`:

```dart
final trimmed = build().applyLocalTrimFallback(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
);
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
return false;
```

`AutoCompactorHooks.onDone` is documented as *"Called once after the loop terminates, on success or exhaustion"*, and the factory's own `ok` branch comments that *"hosts key off [onDone] … a structured run that skips it leaves them open forever"*. Every other terminal path closes it:

- classic `_runPass` failure branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:479-500`): fires `onPass(ok: false)` **and** `onDone`;
- structured `ok` branch and the new trim path: fire `onDone`.

After this change, the timed-out-nothing-droppable path is the **only** terminal path that leaves the bracket open, and it has a concrete CLI consequence: `_AutoCompactorCliHooks.onDone` is what fires `_hep?.compactionEnd(...)` and clears `_runTokensBefore` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:192-207`, set in `onPass:122`, cleared **only** in `onDone:207`). A run that ends here leaves the HEP `compaction_start` bracket unclosed and `_runTokensBefore` stale, so the **next** compaction's freed-delta frame is computed against the failed run's before-count.

The new nothing-droppable test pins this exact path (and already instruments `doneCount`) but never asserts it.

Suggested fix — mirror the classic failure branch (~6 lines):

```dart
if (trimmed) return true;
hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!);
hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(
  pass: adapter.passCount + 1,
  tokensBefore: _requestTokens(),
  tokensAfter: _requestTokens(),
  fallback: null,
  ok: false,
  error: outcome.error,
));
hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens());
return false;
```

…and add `expect(hooks.doneCount, <expected>)` to the second test. Pre-existing gap, so not blocking — but it is a two-line-in-scope fix on a branch this PR owns.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 375

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `applyLocalTrimFallback` reports success unconditionally — consider the under-trigger check `_runPass` uses**

```dart
hooks.onDone(pass, tokensAfter);
return true;
```

The classic trim branch reports success only when the trim actually landed under the compaction trigger (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:478-483`):

```dart
return (
  done: true,
  success:
      !shouldCompact(tokensAfter, window, settings) &&
      !_overMessageCap(),
);
```

The new method returns `true` whenever anything was droppable. By the gh-1425 clamping the token dimension is satisfied in practice, but the gh-1680 **message-cap** dimension is not: a compaction fired by `messageCapTriggerReached` that times out will trim tokens, leave `count ≥ cap − margin` (many tiny kept messages), report success, and the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure), so suggestion-level — but either mirroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional would keep the two valves honest in the same way.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` line 358

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `runToken` cancellation parity — `run()` surfaces a user abort, this new public valve does not**

`AutoCompactor.run()` deliberately rethrows a cancelled run token (issue #1085 round-4):

```dart
} finally {
  // A cancelled compaction is NEVER a mere failed pass …
  runToken?.throwIfCancelled();

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

# pr-1754: gh-1743 [BUG] Structured compaction timeout (300s budget) aborts session instead of falling back to localTrim

## Description

Closes #1743
### Root Cause

When a background structured compaction (`CompactionEngine.structured`) hit its 300s budget watchdog — or a gateway 504/disconnect the engine could not recover from — `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` failed fast (`hooks.onBothRolesFailed` + `return false`) in its `outcome.timedOut` branch (`lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`). The over-window continuation funnel read `false` as "compaction exhausted" and aborted the live task (`the transcript is still ~X tokens vs a Y-token window — N compaction passes did not free it`), even though the session file keeps every record and the classic engine already had a mechanical rescue valve for exactly this situation.

### Fix

- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart`: added `AutoCompactor.applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass})` — applies the same `_localTrimFallback()` valve the classic pass ladder ends on (keeps the most recent `keepRecentTokens`, repairs tool pairing, prefixes the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass receipt and closes the `onDone` bracket exactly once. The factory's `timedOut` branch now applies this fallback instead of aborting the session; the both-roles-failed verdict is kept only when nothing is droppable.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `fix(gh-1743)` entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/agent/auto_compactor_structured_budget_test.dart`:
  - `gh-1743: a factory-level budget timeout (wedged judge past the total budget) falls back to the local trim instead of aborting the session` — reproduction test, **failed before the fix** (`ok: false`), now passes: run rescued, `local-trim` pass receipt reported, `onDone` fired exactly once, live tokens shrank, transcript starts at the `[context trimmed locally` marker, tool pairing intact, all 14 session records preserved.
  - `gh-1743: when nothing is droppable the budget timeout keeps the failure verdict` — pins the honest failure path (no trim → `onBothRolesFailed` + `false`, no live-context change).
- Full suite: 11,926 tests passed / 18 failed / ~62 skipped (`dart test`). All 828 `test/agent/` + `test/compaction/` tests pass. Every one of the 18 failures is in real-process suites (`test/browser_ext/`, `test/integration/`) and was reproduced identically on the untouched baseline commit `806f022` in a clean worktree — pre-existing runner-environment issues (no Chrome/D-Bus; CLI-spawn integration flakiness), unrelated to this change. CI runs those suites in their dedicated workflows/shards.

### Notes

- No behavior change on other timeout shapes: a per-call budget kill the structured engine recovers from (#515/#541) still resolves inside the engine; a non-timeout structured failure still falls through to the classic engine.
- The trim is in-memory only — the session JSONL keeps the full history; the next restart replays it and the pre-flight compaction retries the LLM path.
- The change is additive to the existing fallback contract; no new exports beyond the new public method on the already-exported `AutoCompactor`.

+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry

  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:

  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;

  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via

+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

{"patch":"[lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart#E936]
SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

### Thread 1 (IMPORTANT): close `onDone` bracket on the timed-out + nothing-droppable path
- **RED**: Extend the second test with `expect(hooks.doneCount, 1)` (and also assert a failed pass receipt exists). Currently `doneCount == 0` on that path → test fails.
- **GREEN**: In `AutoCompactorFactory.run()` timedOut branch: after `hooks.onBothRolesFailed(outcome.error!)`, fire `hooks.onPass(AutoCompactorPass(ok: false, ...))` and `hooks.onDone(adapter.passCount + 1, _requestTokens())`, then `return false`. Mirror the classic `_runPass` failure branch.
- Also assert a failed pass receipt in the test: `expect(hooks.passes.where((p) => !p.ok), isNotEmpty)` — check AutoCompactorPass has `error` field.

### Thread 3 (SUGESTION): runToken cancellation parity
- **RED**: New test: factory with a pre-canceled runToken + forced timeout → `run()` throws `CancelledException` and no trim receipt is fired, `bothRolesError` is null (no failure verdict reported either — cancel is not a failed pass), context untouched.

Wait — where should the guard go: top of `applyLocalTrimFallback` or the factory's timedOut branch? The reviewer suggested "a `runToken?.throwIfCancelled()` at the top of the method (or in the factory's timed-out branch)". 

If at the top of `applyLocalTrimFallback`: the exception propagates out of the factory's `run()` (from the timedOut branch). Any future host calling the method directly also gets the belt. This covers both. I'll put it at the top of `applyLocalTrimFallback` with a doc-comment note.

But wait: what does the test expect exactly? In the factory's `run()`:

```dart
if (outcome.timedOut) {
 final trimmed = build().applyLocalTrimFallback(pass: adapter.passCount + 1);
 if (trimmed) return true;
 ...
}
``

If `applyLocalTrimFallback` throws CanceledException, it propagates out of `factory.run()`. The test: `expect(() => factory.run(), throwsA(isA<CancelledException>()))`. Also assert: `hooks.bothRolesError` isNull, no passes, doneCount == 0, and the context untouched (no trim marker).

Hmm — also need to think: with a cancelled runToken, would `_runStructured` even return `timedOut: true`? The runToken cancel is linked into budgetSource. Let me check `_runStructured`'s timeout handling — `running.timeout(totalBudget, ...)`. If the run token is cancelled BEFORE the factory run starts... The structured engine would fail fast on the cancelled budget token (judge call gets cancelled token → failure, not timeout?). Hmm, in that case `outcome.timedOut` might be false and it falls through to the classic engine `build().run()` — which rethrows via its own `finally` `runToken?.throwIfCancelled()`.

To reliably hit `outcome.timedOut == true` with a cancelled runToken in a test, I need the same setup as the existing tests (a judge stream that never settles, totalBudget 300ms) but with `runToken:` pre-canceled (or cancelled just after run starts). 

Hmm — if runToken is cancelled up front, the budget token gets cancelled too (linked in `_runStructured`). Then the judge call receives a cancelled token. The test's mainStream ignores cancelToken and pushes StartEvent immediately... Let me look at what `_runStructured` does — the judge adapter `streamFunctionHideJudge`. If the stream never ends (only StartEvent pushed, no DoneEvent), the judge pends forever regardless of cancel? Actually the existing first test relies on exactly that: "A judge stream that NEVER settles — not even on cancel". And with the budget token cancelled... let me check how `running.timeout` and outcome.timedOut work. Let me read the rest of `_runStructured`.

Actually, the interplay: with runToken cancelled up-front and linked to budgetSource, the judge/sumarizer calls get cancelled tokens. The wedged stream (never settles) → the run pends → `running.timeout(totalBudget)` fires → TimeoutException → outcome.timedOut = true. Then our new guard throws CanceledException. That works.

But hold on — is there anything in the engine that checks `budgetSource.token.isCancelled` and fails fast instead of pending? Let me read the rest of `_runStructured` and the structured engine to be sure. Let me also check `streamFunctionHideJudge`.

### Thread 2 (SUGESTION): document unconditional `true`
- Doc-comment update on `applyLocalTrimFallback` explaining why success is not gated on the under-trigger check (token dimension is clamped by gh-1425; message-cap dimension self-heals at the next pre-flight compaction, which is a healthy LM-backed run; the failure verdict must stay reserved for "nothing was droppable" because returning false here aborts the session — gh-1743's whole point). No behavior change. No new test needed strictly (doc change), but I could... TDD rule says never change production code without a test that reproduces the issue. A doc comment is not production behavior. For the reply I'll cite the updated doc lines.

Hmm, actually — wait. Let me reconsider whether to also mirror the check. The reviewer's concern: "the over-window funnel resumes a run that re-triggers compaction on the very next turn. It is self-limiting (the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure)". 

Hmm, "the next timeout finds nothing droppable → honest failure" — that's about a NEXT timeout. But the next compaction attempt is a normal pre-flight (healthy budget) — it would run the full LM path and compact properly. Only if THAT also wedges past 300s would the trim fire again. OK.

The doc approach is reviewer-sanctioned ("either miroring the `_runPass` check or documenting why the unconditional `true` is intentional"). I'll write the doc comment carefully, cross-referencing `_runPass`'s under-trigger check and gh-1680.

Actually, hmm, let me think about whether miroring is genuinely better. In `_runPass`, success semantics: "the transcript fits in window" — used by the multi-pass ladder to decide whether another pass is needed. `applyLocalTrimFallback` semantics per its doc: "reports whether the live context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable — the caller keeps its failure verdict." The factory's caller (the over-window continuation funnel) reads `true` as "run rescued — resume" and `false` as "compaction exhausted — abort the live task". These are different contracts: the factory result is binary "session lives / session dies", NOT "transcript fits". Returning false when the trim landed but message-cap still trips would kill a session that has a bounded, working context — strictly worse and contrary to the fix's purpose. So documenting is not just acceptable; miroring would be wrong for this valve. 

I'll document this reasoning in the doc comment so the two valves' difference is explicit, and in the reply.

### Thread 4 (SUGESTION): CHANGELOG wording
- Narrow "(300s total, or a provider-level kill the engine cannot recover from)" → "(300s total)". Reword the entry to match the actual `outcome.timedOut` branch. Also the phrase "re-running the classic engine here would only re-wedge the same endpoint" stays fine.

New wording:
``
- fix(gh-1743): a structured compaction that hits its total-budget

process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

flutter analyze+tests;

and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are

SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

{"patch":"[lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart#E936]
SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}

+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).

+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();

+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();

{"patch":"[lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart#E936]
SWAP 349.=361:
+  /// gh-1743: host-callable emergency valve for a timed-out compaction —
+  /// applies the same mechanical local trim [_localTrimFallback] the
+  /// classic pass ladder ends on (keep the most recent
+  /// [CompactionSettings.keepRecentTokens], repair tool pairing, prefix
+  /// the `[context trimmed locally]` marker), fires the `local-trim` pass
+  /// receipt and closes the [AutoCompactorHooks.onDone] bracket exactly
+  /// like the `_runPass` trim branch, and reports whether the live
+  /// context was actually bounded. `false` means nothing was droppable —
+  /// the caller keeps its failure verdict.
+  ///
+  /// Deliberately NOT gated on `_runPass`'s under-trigger check
+  /// (`!shouldCompact && !_overMessageCap`): the gh-1425 clamp lands the
+  /// trim under the TOKEN trigger by construction, so the only dimension
+  /// that can stay over is the gh-1680 message cap (many tiny kept
+  /// messages). This boolean answers "does the session live" for the
+  /// over-window funnel — a `false` here aborts the live task, gh-1743's
+  /// whole bug — and a still-over-cap context self-heals at the next
+  /// turn's pre-flight compaction, which fires on the message-cap
+  /// dimension and runs the healthy LM path. A cancelled [runToken]
+  /// throws before anything is trimmed or reported (issue #1085 cancel
+  /// parity with [run]).
+  bool applyLocalTrimFallback({int pass = 1}) {
+    // Cancel parity (issue #1085): a cancelled compaction is NEVER a
+    // mere failed pass. If the owning run's token cancelled around the
+    // moment the budget fired, surface the abort instead of trimming —
+    // and reporting success on — a run the user stopped.
+    runToken?.throwIfCancelled();
+    final tokensBefore = _requestTokens();
+    final trimmed = _localTrimFallback();
+    if (trimmed == null) return false;"}
